stack: ROCm 7.0.2 with its ASan runtime libraries
PyTorch 2.10.0 built from source with -fsanitize=address for gfx950:xnack+
runs.run_mode: aorta run --sanitizer asan, proposed in PR #567 (in review, not yet merged)
covered: Global-memory reads and writes in PyTorch's own kernels, because this PyTorch is built with ASan
Global-memory reads and writes in HIP kernels built with ASan
Each error is reported with the kernel, the access, and how far it fell outside which allocation
not_covered: hipBLASLt GEMM kernels: generated assembly that ASan can't instrument, even in an ASan build of hipBLASLt
Shared memory (LDS) inside PyTorch's kernels: this build turns off ASan's LDS lowering, without which some PyTorch softmax kernels fail to launch on gfx950
hipMallocManaged memory, and accesses far outside an allocation
notes: PyTorch's kernels are checked only because PyTorch is built with ASan: with the stock PyTorch wheel the same gpu_smoke run checks 0 of its 3 kernels (measured 2026-10-20), since the wheel ships device code without ASan.
aorta run has no option for workload configuration yet, and hrx must be built for gfx950 on MI350, so the hrx rows ran through the same run-mode entry point from Python, with the configuration shown.
A pass covers what ASan instruments, not every access.
